author: Afḍal al-Dīn Abū Ḥāmid Muḥammad al-Iṣfahānī (Turka)
edition: Āshtiyānī, Tamhīd al-Qawāʿid, 1360 SH (printed pp. 48–60), accessible electronic transcription
english_reference: Joseph E. B. Lumbard, 'Establishing the Principles', Anthology of Philosophy in Persia IV, pp. 464–479. Consulted only as translation comparator.
segmentation: Only strings explicitly introduced by قال and separated from Ibn Turka's أقول are included. Numbering and headings are editorial. Gaps between matn loci contain commentary, not necessarily lost matn.

units.title: Opening: the problem of tawḥīd
units.arabic: الحمد لوليّه، والصلاة على نبيّه محمد وآله. وبعد، فإن تقرير مسألة التوحيد على النحو الذي ذهب إليه العارفون، وأشار إليه المحقّقون، من المسائل الغامضة التي لا يصل إليها أفكار علماء الناظرين المجادلين، ولا يدركها أذهان الفضلاء الباحثين من الناظرين.
units.english: Praise belongs to His walī, and blessings be upon His Prophet Muḥammad and his family. To proceed: setting forth the question of divine unity in the form maintained by the gnostics and intimated by those who have realized the truth is among the difficult questions beyond the thought of disputatious scholars engaged in speculative inquiry and beyond the comprehension of accomplished investigators among the speculative thinkers.
notes: The initial walī (وليّه) is left transliterated because its precise referent is contested by the context. Lumbard renders the expression interpretively as a reference to a vicegerent; Ibn Turka's subsequent explanation links the formula to universal existence and the manifestation of perfection.
Muḥaqqiqūn is translated contextually as 'those who have realized the truth,' not simply 'researchers'; the matn deliberately contrasts such people with the ahl al-naẓar.
These words belong to Abū Ḥāmid's matn: the commentary introduces them with قال and resumes with أقول.

units.title: The opponent's physiological objection
units.arabic: فإن الأكثرين منهم يزعمون أن القطع بها يدلّ على استحكام سوء المزاج في موضوعات القوى النفسانية، وعلى احتراق الموادّ الصالحة البدنيّة، واستيلاء المرّة السوداء على الأعضاء الشريفة الأصليّة؛ إذ القطع ببطلان جميع الأحكام العقليّة والحسّيّة والفطريّة والغريزيّة عقيب ارتكاب المجاهدات والرياضات الجزافيّة الصادرة عن الوساوس الخياليّة لا يمكن لأحد إلا عند عروض ذلك السبب الحديث وابتلائه بما ذكرنا من المرض الخبيث.
units.english: For most of them suppose that being certain of it indicates that a disordered temperament has become firmly established in the bodily substrates of the faculties of the soul, that the sound bodily materials have been burnt up, and that black bile has gained ascendancy over the principal noble organs. For, they argue, after undertaking arbitrary struggles and disciplines prompted by imaginational misgivings, no one could become certain that all judgments of intellect, sense, innate disposition, and natural instinct are invalid unless such a newly arising cause had intervened and the person had contracted the grievous disorder just mentioned.
notes: **Attribution:** this presents the opponents' objection, not the author's own assessment. The later sharḥ explicitly explains that Abū Ḥāmid first states the adversary's argument at its strongest.
**Variant:** Āshtiyānī's electronic transcription prints احتراق, with احتراف registered as a variant. The translation provisionally follows احتراق ('burning up').
موضوعات القوى النفسانية refers to the bodily substrates/organs of the psychological faculties, not to the 'subjects' of propositions.

units.title: Reply to the objection
units.arabic: لكن لمّا كان الأمر على خلاف ما ظنّوه، بل على عكس ما تخيّلوه.
units.english: Yet the matter is contrary to what they have supposed—indeed, the very reverse of what they have imagined.
notes: The author announces his reversal succinctly. The commentary's long discussion of faculties and their natural end is not included here, in accordance with the matn-first editorial boundary.

units.title: Purpose and method of the treatise
units.arabic: أردت أن أكتب رسالة أوضح فيها حقّيّة مذهب العارفين، وبطلان قول الطاعنين من المنكرين، مشتملة على صفوة ما ظهر لي من الحدس في هذه المسألة، ومحتوية على زبدة ما انتهى إليه نظري في تلك المعركة. وأردنا أن نقرّر تلك المسألة على طريق المناظرين، وأن نسلك مسلك المناظرة مع الطاعنين، ونثبتها بحجج قويّة ندفع بها عنها طعن المنكرين، ونشدّ بها رغبة الطالبين. اللهم اجعلنا من زمرة الناجين الفائزين دون الضالّين المردودين. يا إخوان التحصيل، سارعوا إلى تحصيل الكمال الحقيقي والبقاء الأبدي قبل أن يتسارع إليكم الفناء الضروري والفوت البدني، وبادروا في حياتكم قبل أن يتبادر إليكم الموت الطبيعي، واستعينوا به في كلّ الأمور، وتوكّلوا عليه إن كنتم مؤمنين.
units.english: I have resolved to compose a treatise explaining the truth of the gnostics' doctrine and the falsity of the deniers' attacks, bringing together the choicest insights that intellectual intuition has disclosed to me concerning this question and the quintessence of what my reflective inquiry has reached in this controversy. We have chosen to formulate the question in the manner of disputants, to enter into debate with the critics, and to establish it through forceful proofs that repel their objections and strengthen the seekers' desire. O God, place us among those who are saved and victorious, not among those who are lost and rejected. Brothers engaged in the acquisition of knowledge: hasten to attain true perfection and everlasting abiding before inevitable perishing and bodily dissolution overtake you. Make use of your life before natural death comes upon you. Seek His aid in every affair, and place your trust in Him, if you are believers.
notes: **Variants:** حقّيّة / حقيقة; من الحدس / بالحدس; أردنا / رأينا; المناظرين / الناظرين; نشدّ / تشتدّ. Base readings have been retained, not silently harmonized.
حدس is the technical ḥads of the philosophical psychology and logic of discovery. It is not translated simply as 'mystical inspiration'; نظري is deliberate rational inquiry.
The phrase 'we have chosen' represents the manuscript's move from first-person singular to plural, retained in the English.

units.title: Existence is common in meaning
units.arabic: اعلم أن الوجود مشترك بين الوجودات الخاصّة كلّها، لا بحسب اللفظ بل بحسب المعنى، كما بيّنّاه في سائر كتبنا.
units.english: Know that existence is common to all particular existences—not merely in respect of the word, but in respect of the meaning—as we have explained in our other writings.
notes: Crucial lexical decision: مشترك بين ... بحسب المعنى expresses commonality of meaning, not composition out of particular existences. Lumbard's phrasing here could be read more mereologically; the Arabic and Ibn Turka's ensuing explanation concern الاشتراك.
The general claim of a common meaning is not yet, taken alone, a demonstration that extramental existence is numerically one.
The section heading is editorial, not part of Abū Ḥāmid's matn; Lumbard's note reports that Āshtiyānī inserted it.

units.title: The necessity of existence
units.arabic: ومن البيّن أن حقيقته من حيث هي هي لا يقبل العدم لذاتها، لامتناع اتّصاف أحد النقيضين بالآخر، وامتناع انقلاب طبيعة إلى طبيعة الآخر؛ ومتى امتنع العدم عليها لذاتها كانت واجبة لذاتها.
units.english: It is evident that the reality of existence, considered precisely as itself, does not admit nonexistence in virtue of its own essence: one contradictory cannot possess the qualification of the other, nor can one nature be transformed into the nature of its opposite. Whenever nonexistence is intrinsically impossible for it, it is necessary in itself.
notes: The sequence of proof is: impossibility of intrinsic nonexistence → intrinsic necessity. Whether this proceeds validly from the concept of existence to real necessity is a philosophical question, not an editorially settled fact.

**Unresolved agreement:** the digital Arabic prints لا يقبل after the feminine حقيقة, then لذاتها. The masculine verb may reflect an attraction to الوجود or a transmitted/typographic inconsistency; preserved here instead of silently emending to لا تقبل.
The separate arguments for necessity following أقول are Ibn Turka's commentary, not this ancestor's matn.
